title: Sheinbaum Asks Xi to Send Another Panda to Mexico for Chapultepec Zoo
author: Redacción/SinEmbargo
content:
_This article
by[Redacción/SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/)
originally appeared in the [November 17, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4905234/sheinbaum-pide-a-xi-enviar-otro-
oso-panda-a-mexico-para-el-zoologico-de-chapultepec/), a Mexican digital news
outlet._

_Chapultepec Zoo is currently home to Xin Xin, a 36-year-old female who is the
only known giant panda not owned by China._

**Mexico City, November 17 (SinEmbargo).-** Mexico’s president, [**Claudia
Sheinbaum Pardo**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4905065/sheinbaum-inaugura-nueva-
era-mexico-china-tras-su-encuentro-con-xi-jinping/), revealed that she
formally asked **Xi Jinping** , her Chinese counterpart, for another panda for
**Chapultepec Zoo** , during their first bilateral meeting and ahead of the 55
years of diplomatic relations that the two countries will celebrate in 2027.

The request was made during the meeting held in **Shenzhen** , on the
sidelines of the **Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC)** summit. After
the meeting, [Sheinbaum](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4904524/csp-se-reune-con-
mexicanos-en-china-son-extraordinarios-y-un-orgullo-para-el-pais/) explained
to the media that they had discussed making progress on tourism issues as part
of the bilateral relationship.

> “We discussed making progress on tourism issues; we also asked him for a
> panda for Chapultepec Zoo as part of this relationship,” the president said.

The president linked the request to the anniversary of Mexico-China relations
and the push for a “new era” of cooperation. The two leaders also discussed
collaboration in science, technology, the environment, health (including smart
hospitals), infrastructure, agriculture, clean energy, trade (with an emphasis
on increasing Mexican exports such as avocados and tequila) and tourism.

> [Post by @Claudiashein on
> X](https://x.com/Claudiashein/status/2122616597814956234)

## Xin Xin, Chapultepec’s Last Panda

Chapultepec Zoo is currently home to Xin Xin, a **36-year-old female who is
the only known giant panda not owned by China**. She is the last descendant of
the line of pandas that arrived in Mexico in 1975, when the Chinese government
gave the pair Pe Pe and Ying Ying as a gesture of friendship.

Beginning in the 1980s, China changed its policy and generally lends pandas
for set periods in exchange for payments earmarked for the conservation of the
species in the wild, instead of giving them away permanently.

Xin Xin was born on July 1, 1990, and is the daughter of the iconic panda
Tohuí. Considered a wildlife ambassador, she has far surpassed her species’
life expectancy in the wild, between 20 and 25 years, thanks to the work of
veterinarians, biologists, nutritionists and keepers at the capital’s
conservation center.

In July 2026, the Chapultepec Wildlife Conservation Center celebrated her 36th
birthday, a celebration that coincided with the facility’s 103rd anniversary.
Its cornerstone was laid on July 6, 1923, by Mexican biologist and naturalist
Alfonso L. Herrera. The center is currently home to more than 1,200 animals
from more than 200 species.

![Xin Xin leans toward a decorated birthday cake at Chapultepec
Zoo.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/sheinbaum-panda-
chapultepec-inline-1.jpg)Mexican panda Xin Xin celebrated her 36th birthday at
the Chapultepec Wildlife Conservation Center. Photo: Galo Cañas, Cuartoscuro.

## Sheinbaum Ushers in a “New Era” in Mexico-China Relations

President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (CSP) said that her visit to China
represents “a new era in relations between Mexico and China,” following a
bilateral meeting with her Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, during the 33rd
Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting, being held
in Shenzhen.

During the meeting, the two leaders highlighted the importance of the bonds of
friendship between their countries and expressed their willingness to continue
strengthening them through the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, a
mechanism for political, diplomatic and economic understanding established in
2013.

> “This visit represents a new era in relations between Mexico and China, a
> relationship that is the result of deep bonds of friendship and shared
> principles, such as cooperation for development and shared prosperity,”
> Sheinbaum Pardo said.

The head of the executive branch noted that Mexico and China have expanded
their areas of cooperation in different fields, including sargassum
mitigation, science and technology, infrastructure, agriculture, clean energy,
water resources, health, culture and tourism.

_-With information from Xinhua_
